items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: oh they got Red Allen, Higginbotham, oh they were all there

ctx.x: Well I’m a veteran of the Metropole. In 1958, 7 or 8, is when we started pushing the shipyard. And I bid on some ocean going freighters and passenger ships for three lines in

New York, U.S. Lines, Moore McCormick and American Export. And I had to work the Maritime Commission in Washington as well. So I was on a schedule to take me to the east coast two and three times a week. When I was in New York what was involved was going down in the morning, down to where all the marine activity is, calling on somebody, having a drunken lunch with them, and then going back to the hotel to take a nap, and then spend the evening at the place, at the Metropole there.
